summary: Iteration 11 e2e testing complete for Admin Console RBAC, user/workspace suspension, and new nav/auth-page links. Backend: 23/23 pytest cases passed (admin GET RBAC for 8 endpoints allow-admin + forbid-non-admin, anonymous 401, global-blocklist POST/DELETE + validation, user suspend blocks login and unsuspend restores, admin self-modify guard 400, last-admin demotion guard, workspace suspension blocks redirect and restore resumes it, plus cleanup safety net). Frontend: new nav-contact-link and auth-back-home-link verified and route to /contact and / respectively. AdminRoute correctly redirects non-admin (teammate) from /admin to /app while admin session renders the Admin Console with all required data-testid nav items, admin-stats, users/workspaces tabs and suspend switches. All suspensions were restored after tests.

minor.issue: Baseline redirect returns 200 (security 'challenge' page) instead of 302 for typical requests originating from our test host — traffic is scored ≥30 and requires challenge even when link protection is off. Not a bug per-spec (challenge is by design for workspace-level rules), but any automated integration client hitting /api/r must handle the 200 challenge branch.

_suspended_workspaces cache TTL is 30s, so a freshly-suspended workspace can still 302-redirect for up to 30s. Consider invalidating the set on suspend/unsuspend (similar to invalidate_cache/invalidate_rules) for immediate effect.

integration_issues.issue: Nav links use raw <a href="/contact"> which triggers a full-page reload rather than react-router client navigation. Works correctly but is inconsistent with the login/register buttons that use navigate(); minor UX/perf.

action_items: (Optional) In backend/app/domains/admin.py PATCH /workspaces/{id}, invalidate the redirect._WS_SUSPENDED cache immediately after toggling (currently relies on 30s TTL).
(Optional) In PublicNav.jsx, switch nav <a href> to react-router <Link to> for SPA-consistent navigation on the Contact link (and siblings).
(Optional) Add data-testid=admin-console-users-list to the users table so tests can wait deterministically for the users query to resolve before probing user-suspend-* switches.
critical_code_review_comments: admin.py PATCH /users/{id} correctly guards self-mutation (400) and last-admin demotion — verified.
auth.py login() gates suspended accounts before issuing tokens (returns 403 with descriptive message) — verified.

redirect.py _suspended_workspaces() uses a 30s TTL cache; suspension takes up to 30s to take effect. Tests handle this by polling — but for production admins, an explicit cache-invalidation call on PATCH would be safer.
admin.py add_global uses ipaddress.ip_network/ip_address for validation — good. Also invalidates the global block cache on add/delete.
AdminRoute.jsx cleanly handles the three states (loading spinner, unauthenticated -> /login, non-admin -> /app). Good.
PublicNav.jsx uses <a href> for links (causing full page reload). Consider react-router Link for consistency.

The workspace-suspension test polls up to 35s for redirect state to flip in each direction because of the 30s _WS_SUSPENDED TTL cache. If timing gets flaky, extend deadline. rca of the issue: N/A — all Iteration 11 acceptance criteria pass. Only two minor observations: (a) redirect challenge-vs-302 for scored traffic (design), (b) 30s cache lag on workspace-suspend propagation to the redirect service (mitigation: emit explicit cache invalidation in PATCH /admin/workspaces).
